'''Gershon Kurizki'''  ({{Langx|he|גרשון קוריצקי}}; born October 29, 1952) is a theoretical quantum physicist, known for his contributions to the fields of [[Quantum optics|quantum light-matter interaction]], [[Quantum control|control of quantum system]] interactions with the environment, [[quantum thermodynamics]] and quantum measurement theory. Since 1997 he has been a professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], [[Israel]], where he is still actively engaged in research as professor emeritus. He has so far coauthored more than 320 research articles,<ref name="Scholar2">{{cite web |title=Gershon Kurizki |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=RkrJ0LsAAAAJ&hl=iw&oi=ao |website=Google Scholar}}</ref> among those over 60 articles in high-profile journals (Nature, Science Advances, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Nature Communications, Physical Review Letters) and two books. His work has been cited to date more than 15,830 times on Google Scholar, giving him an h-index of 66 as of September 2026.<ref name="Scholar2" />

Gershon Kurizki has published poetry and philosophical essays in literary and philosophical magazines and books. His book "The Quantum Matrix" ([[Oxford University Press]], 2020) renders scientific, philosophical and poetic descriptions of the world.

==Biography==
Gershon Kurizki was born in 1952 in [[Vilnius]], Lithuania (then the Soviet Union).<ref name=":22">{{cite web |url=https://aias.au.dk/fileadmin/www.aias.au.dk/Hosted_events/Kurizki_Gershon_CV.pdf |title=Gershon Kurizki - Curriculum Vitae |website=Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies |access-date=November 5, 2024}}</ref> He immigrated to Israel with his family in 1960. After completing his B.Sc. and M.Sc. in physics at the [[Technion]] in 1979, he moved in 1980 to the [[University of New Mexico]], USA, where he obtained his Ph. D in physics in 1983.{{Citation needed|date=November 2024}} His doctoral thesis, written under the supervision of [[Marlan Scully]] and John McIver, was on radiation from fast-charged particles in crystals.

He was appointed lecturer at [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1983.<ref name=":22" /> He subsequently moved to the [[Weizmann Institute]] where he was appointed senior scientist in 1987, associate professor with tenure in 1991 and professor in 1997.<ref name=":12">{{cite web |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kurizki_Gershon |title=Gershon Kurizki - Member Profile |website=Academia Europaea |access-date=November 5, 2024}}</ref> From 1996 to 2024 he held the Dunne Professorial Chair in Quantum Optics at the Weizmann Institute. Throughout the years, he served as visiting professor at the Universities of [[Aarhus University|Aarhus]] in Denmark, [[Ulm University|Ulm]] and [[Heidelberg University|Heidelberg]] in Germany, and [[Shanghai University|Shanghai]] in China.<ref name=":12" />

He coordinated 3 multi-national EU projects and participated in multiple US (NSF-sponsored) and European, particularly German (DFG-sponsored) projects. He delivered invited or plenary talks at ca. 350 conferences and workshops worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GPOLC2025 {{!}} Optics Conference {{!}} Photonics {{!}} Lasers {{!}} Nice {{!}} France {{!}} Top conferences in Optics {{!}} Conferences in Europe {{!}} September {{!}} Meeting {{!}} Summit {{!}} Registration {{!}} Abstract {{!}} Call for Papers |url=https://gpolc2025.synergiasummits.com/plenary-speakers |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=gpolc2025.synergiasummits.com}}</ref>

His editorial service has included a term as Topical Editor of the Journal of Physics B and of Optics Letters from 2000 to 2012 and, since 2023, a seat on the Advisory Board of Applied Physics Letters, Quantum.<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last1=Ph.D |last2=Science |first2=Chair at Weizmann Institute of |title=Gershon KURIZKI {{!}} Chair {{!}} Ph.D {{!}} Weizmann Institute of Science, Reẖovot {{!}} weizmann {{!}} Department of Chemical Physics {{!}} Research profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gershon-Kurizki |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=ResearchGate |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Akulin |first1=V M |last2=Kurizki |first2=G |last3=Lidar |first3=D A |date=2007-05-14 |title=How to control decoherence and entanglement in quantum complex systems? |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0953-4075/40/9/E01 |journal=Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics |volume=40 |issue=9 |doi=10.1088/0953-4075/40/9/E01 |bibcode=2007JPhB...40.....A |issn=0953-4075}}</ref>

Over a research career spanning more than four decades, his laboratory has trained 36 postdoctoral researchers and 21 PhD students, eleven of the latter receiving distinction awards from the Weizmann Institute; roughly two-thirds of his former trainees have gone on to academic positions of their own. His research today continues through an international network of collaborators spanning Austria, the Czech Republic, Greece, Germany, India, Italy, Lithuania, Spain, Turkey, and the United States.<ref name="Website-1" />

Among his former trainees are academics such as Nir Bar-Gill, Miriam Blaauboer, Arnab Chakrabarti, Ze Cheng, Bimalendu Deb, Arnab Ghosh, David Gelbwaser-Klimovsky, Yonathan Japha, Igor Mazets, Avijit Misra, Victor Mukherjee, Goren Gordon, Duncan O'Dell, Tomáš Opatrný, David Petrosyan and Ephraim Shahmoon.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Group Members {{!}} Prof. Gershon Kurizki |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/chembiophys/gershon/group-members |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=www.weizmann.ac.il |language=en}}</ref>

Gershon Kurizki is married to Zipora (Zipi, nee Zmishlany). He has two sons, Naham (b. 1978) and Yodan (b. 1986).<ref name=":22" />

==Research==
===Quantum Zeno and Anti-Zeno control===
Kurizki and coworkers developed a theory of decay and decoherence control<ref name="universal2">{{cite journal |last1=Kofman |first1=A.G. |last2=Kurizki |first2=G. |title=Universal dynamical control of quantum mechanical decay: modulation of the coupling to the continuum|journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2001 |volume=87|issue=27 |article-number=270405|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.270405|pmid=11800864 |arxiv=quant-ph/0107076 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..87A0405K }}</ref><ref name="unified2">{{cite journal |last1=Kofman |first1=A.G. |title=Unified theory of dynamically suppressed qubit decoherence in thermal baths |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2004 |volume=93 |issue=13 |article-number=130406 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.130406|pmid=15524688 |bibcode=2004PhRvL..93m0406K }}</ref> that exploits two opposing universal effects. One is the [[quantum Zeno effect]] (QZE) of decay slowdown, whereas the other one is its inverse, the anti-Zeno effect (AZE) of decay speedup.<ref name="acceleration2">{{cite journal |last1=Kofman |first1=A.G. |last2=Kurizki |first2=G. |title=Acceleration of quantum decay processes by frequent observations |journal=Nature |date=2000 |volume=405 |issue=6786 |pages=546–550 |doi=10.1038/35014537|pmid=10850708 |bibcode=2000Natur.405..546K }}</ref> They showed that both effects, originally thought to be caused by frequent measurements of the system, arise under any form of frequent control. Their discovery of occurrence of the AZE was deemed counterintuitive and referred to as "a watched pot boils quicker".<ref name="Milonni2">{{cite journal |last1=Milonni |first1=P.W. |title=A watched pot boils quicker |journal= Nature|date=2000 |volume=405 |issue=6786 |page=525 |doi=10.1038/35014719|pmid=10850699 |bibcode=2000Natur.405..525M }}</ref> In their theory, both the QZE and the AZE are obtained from the universal Kofman-Kurizki (KK) formula for decay and decoherence control, which has been experimentally tested in diverse systems and has influenced the development of control strategies in quantum information processing. This formula has shown that the QZE is key to the protection of quantum information from decoherence, whereas the AZE can facilitate the resetting of an [[open quantum system]] to its initial state following a [[quantum operation]]. Kurizki and coworkers showed that the AZE can yield a quantum advantage in the performance of fast-driven heat machines.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Victor |last2=Kofman |first2=Abraham G. |last3=Kurizki |first3=Gershon |date=2020-01-10 |title=Anti-Zeno quantum advantage in fast-driven heat machines |journal=Communications Physics |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=8 |doi=10.1038/s42005-019-0272-z |doi-access=free |arxiv=1905.00665 |bibcode=2020CmPhy...3....8M |issn=2399-3650}}</ref> They experimentally showed that the QZE can probe quantum noise properties of photons.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Virzì |first1=Salvatore |last2=Avella |first2=Alessio |last3=Piacentini |first3=Fabrizio |last4=Gramegna |first4=Marco |last5=Opatrný |first5=Tomáš |last6=Kofman |first6=Abraham G. |last7=Kurizki |first7=Gershon |last8=Gherardini |first8=Stefano |last9=Caruso |first9=Filippo |last10=Degiovanni |first10=Ivo Pietro |last11=Genovese |first11=Marco |date=2022-07-13 |title=Quantum Zeno and Anti-Zeno Probes of Noise Correlations in Photon Polarization |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.030401 |journal=Physical Review Letters |publisher=American Physical Society |volume=129 |issue=3 |article-number=030401 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.030401 |pmid=35905356 |bibcode=2022PhRvL.129c0401V |arxiv=2103.03698 }}</ref> They also proposed the protection of quantum transport in dissipative media by an effect akin to the QZE.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chakrabarti |first1=Arnab |last2=Ash === Control of quantum thermodynamics and thermal machines ===
Kurizki and coworkers showed the ability to control via the QZE and the AZE the temperature and entropy of open quantum systems:<ref name="control2">{{cite journal |last1=Erez |first1=N. |last2=Gordon |first2=G. |last3=Nest |first3=M. |last4=Kurizki |first4=G. |title=Thermodynamic control by frequent quantum measurements |journal=Nature |date=2008 |volume=452 |issue=7188 |pages=724–727 |doi=10.1038/nature06873|pmid=18401404 |arxiv=0804.2178 |bibcode=2008Natur.452..724E }}</ref> the QZE has been shown to heat up the system and the AZE to cool it down. This approach, referred to as "frequent measurements turn up the heat",<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chapin |first1=K.R. |last2=Scully |first2=M.O. |title=Observations turn up the heat |journal= Nature|date=2008 |volume=452 |issue=7188 |pages=705–706 |doi=10.1038/452705a|pmid=18401399 }}</ref><ref name="watching2">{{cite journal |last1=Ball |first1=P. |title=When watching boils the pot |journal=Nature |date=2000 |doi=10.1038/news000601-9}}</ref> has been experimentally employed to cool down (purify) thermal nuclear spin ensembles in solids.<ref name="anti zeno2">{{cite journal |last1=Dasani |first1=D.B.R. |last2=Yang |first2=S. |last3=Chakrabarti |first3=A. |last4=Finkler |first4=A. |last5=Kurizki |first5=G. |last6=Wrachtrup |first6=J. |title=Anti-Zeno purification of spin baths by quantum probe measurements |journal=Nature Communications |date=2022 |volume=13 |issue=1 |page=7527 |doi=10.18419/darus-3262|pmid=36473849 |pmc=9726817 }}</ref><ref name="masers2">{{cite journal |last1=Ghosh |first1=A. |last2=Gelbwaser-Klimovsky |first2=D. |last3=Niedenzu |first3=W. |last4=Lvovsky |first4=A.I. |last5=Mazets |first5=I. |last6=Scully |first6=M.O. |last7=Kurizki |first7=G. |title=Two-level masers as heat-to-work converters |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=2018 |volume=115 |issue=40 |pages=9941–9944 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1805354115|doi-access=free |pmid=30228114 |pmc=6176601 |arxiv=1712.08936 |bibcode=2018PNAS..115.9941G }}</ref> Kurizki and coworkers revealed the hitherto unnoticed hindering of quantum network purification by symmetry among its constituents and the ability to remove this hindering by symmetry breaking.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sur |first1=Saikat |last2=Chattopadhyay |first2=Pritam |last3=Chakrabarti |first3=Arnab |last4=Palaiodimopoulos |first4=Nikolaos E. |last5=Müstecaplıoğlu |first5=Özgür E. |last6=Finkler |first6=Amit |last7=Rao Dasari |first7=Durga Bhaktavatsala |last8=Kurizki |first8=Gershon |date=2026-04-17 |title=Collective purification of interacting quantum networks beyond symmetry constraints |journal=npj Quantum Information |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=109 |doi=10.1038/s41534-026-01228-9 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2603.03917 |bibcode=2026npjQI..12..109S |issn=2056-6387}}</ref>

Kurizki and coworkers explored the thermodynamics of quantum systems under frequent control.  As part of this approach  they proposed the (minimal) quantum heat engine or refrigerator based on a single two-level atom.<ref name="minimal2">{{cite journal |last1=Gelbwaser-Klimovsky |first1=D. |last2=Alicki |first2=R. |last3=Kurizki |first3=G. |title=Minimal universal quantum heat machine |journal=Physical Review E |date=2013 |volume=87 |issue=1 |article-number=012140 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.87.012140|pmid=23410316 |arxiv=1209.1190 |bibcode=2013PhRvE..87a2140G }}</ref> They showed that if the energy is supplied to the engine by a non-thermal bath, the engine efficiency can surpass the canonical Carnot limit and not adhere to the second law of thermodynamics.<ref name="engine2">{{cite journal |last1=Niedenzu |first1=W. |last2=Mukherjee |first2=V. |last3=Ghosh |first3=A. |last4=Kofman |first4=A.G. |last5=Kurizki |first5=G. |title=Quantum engine efficiency bound beyond the second law of thermodynamics |journal=Nature Communications |date=2018 pmid=36608121 | pmc=9821940 | bibcode=2023SciA....9F1070O }}</ref> They proposed the exotic possibility of driving the heat engine of a spaceship by radiation from a black hole.<ref>{{Cite journal ===Quantum noise sensing under control===
Kurizki and coworkers developed an approach to quantum sensing that eludes the customary definitions of signal and noise. Unlike traditional sensing that aims at suppressing noise while retaining noise-free signals, their sensing focuses on bath-induced noise recorded by a quantum probe under frequent control. They showed that such noise carries information which can identify the processes that generate the noise.<ref name="maximizing2">{{cite journal |last1=Zwick |first1=A. |last2=Álvarez |first2=G.A. |last3=Kurizki |first3=G. |title=Maximizing Information on the Environment by Dynamically Controlled Qubit Probes |journal=Physical Review Applied |date=2016 |volume=5 |issue=1 |article-number=014007 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevApplied.5.014007|arxiv=1507.03281 |bibcode=2016PhRvP...5a4007Z }}</ref> This noise-sensing approach is finding growing applications in biomedical diagnostics. Their colloquial summary of this approach is "the bath is more a friend than a foe". Among its applications for quantum sensing, they identified the ability of noise to provide information on quantum networks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chattopadhyay |first1=Pritam |last2=Misra |first2=Avijit |last3=Sur |first3=Saikat |last4=Petrosyan |first4=David |last5=Kurizki |first5=Gershon |date=2025-10-01 |title=Sensing multiatom networks in cavities via photon-induced excitation resonance |journal=Quantum Science and Technology |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=035006 |doi=10.1088/2058-9565/adcae3 |arxiv=2411.09465 |bibcode=2025QS&T...10c5006C |issn=2058-9565}}</ref>

===Quantum hybrid systems===
Kurizki developed an approach that is being increasingly employed in quantum information processing: the use of quantum hybrid systems consisting of diverse modules, each performing a specific task suited for the advantageous functionality of that module.<ref name="technologies2">{{cite journal |last1=Kurizki |first1=G. |last2=Bertet |first2=P. |last3=Kubo |first3=Y. |last4=Mølmer |first4=K. |last5=Petrosyan |first5=D. |last6=Rabl |first6=P. |last7=Schmiedmayer |first7=J. |title=Quantum technologies with hybrid systems |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=2014 |volume=112 |issue=13 |pages=3866–3873 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1419326112|doi-access=free |pmid=25737558 |pmc=4386362 |arxiv=1504.00158 }}</ref>

===Engineering macroscopic forces by quantum electrodynamics===
Kurizki and coworkers showed that macroscopic forces between dipoles can be "engineered" by controlling the geometry of the quantum vacuum bath that confines them. Their notable discoveries within this approach include the generation of gravitational-like interactions in ultracold gases{{R|technologies}} and giant long-range interactions of photons or dipoles in [[waveguides]].<ref name="BEC2">{{cite journal |last1=O'Dell |first1=D. |last2=Giovanazzi |first2=S. |last3=Kurizki |first3=G. |last4=Akulin |first4=V.M. |title=Bose-Einstein Condensates with 1/r Interatomic Attraction: Electromagnetically Induced "Gravity" |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2000 |volume=84 |issue=25 |pages=5687–5690 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.84.5687|pmid=10991032 |arxiv=quant-ph/9912097 |bibcode=2000PhRvL..84.5687O }}</ref><ref name="vacuum2">{{cite journal |last1=Shahmoon |first1=E. |last2=Mazets |first2=I. |last3=Kurizki |first3=G. |title=Giant vacuum forces via transmission lines |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=2014 |volume=111 |issue=29 |pages=10485–10490 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1401346111|doi-access=free |pmid=25002503 |pmc=4115521 |arxiv=1304.2028 |bibcode=2014PNAS..11110485S }}</ref> These indicate that quantum electrodynamic effects, commonly associated with atomic scales, can be manifested and controlled also at macroscopic scales.<ref name="Casimir2">{{cite journal |last1=Fitzgerald |first1=R.J. |title=Quantum optics, thermodynamics and open systems |journal=Physics Today |date=2014 |volume=67 |doi=10.1063/PT.3.2467}}</ref>

===Measurements for probing and engineering quantum states and correlations===
Kurizki and coworkers explored measuring the state of one of two coupled quantum systems as a means of engineering the state of the other. They showed that arbitrary quantum states of a light beam can be engineered by measuring atoms coupled to it<ref name="generation2">{{cite journal |last1=Garraway |first1=B.M. |last2=Sherman |first2=B. |last3=Moya-Cessa |first3=A. |last4=Knight |first4=P.L. |last5=Kurizki |first5=G. |title=Generation and detection of nonclassical field states by conditional measurements following two-photon resonant interactions |journal=Physical Review A |date=1994 |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=535–547 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.49.535|pmid=9910259 |bibcode=1994PhRvA..49..535G }}</ref> or by counting the photons of another light beam correlated to it.<ref name="teleportation2">{{cite journal |last1=Opatrný |first1=T. |last2=Kurizki |first2=G. |last3=Welsch |first3=D.G. |title=Improvement on teleportation of continuous variables by photon subtraction via conditional measurement |journal=Physical Review A |date=2000 |volume=61 |issue=3 |article-number=032302 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.61.032302|arxiv=quant-ph/9907048 |bibcode=2000PhRvA..61c2302O }}</ref> They developed methods for measuring and quantifying quantum correlations of the kind discovered by [[Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox|Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen]] (EPR) in cold gases.<ref name="matter wave2">{{cite journal |last1=Opatrný |first1=T. |last2=Kurizki |first2=G. |title=Matter-Wave Entanglement and Teleportation by Molecular Dissociation and Collisions |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=2001 |volume=86 |issue=14 |pages=3180–3183 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.3180|pmid=11290137 |arxiv=quant-ph/0009121 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..86.3180O }}</ref> and in dissociating molecules.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sur |first1=Saikat |last2=Chattopadhyay |first2=Pritam |last3=Kurizki |first3=Gershon |date=2025-08-07 |title=Molecular Processes as Quantum Information Resources |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=163 |issue=5 |pages=050901 |doi=10.1063/5.0272970 |pmid=40748089 |arxiv=2508.02597 |bibcode=2025JChPh.163e0901S |issn=0021-9606}}</ref>

* Fellow, [[American Physical Society]] (2002)<ref name="APS2">{{cite web |last1=Gershon |first1=Kurizki |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?award_fellowship%5Bquery%5D=gershon%20kurizki}}</ref>
* The W.E. Lamb Medal for [[Laser science|Laser Science]] and Quantum Optics (Physics of Quantum Electronics, USA) (2008)<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2008 Willis E. Lamb Award |url=https://www.lambaward.com/winners/2008 |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=Lamb Award |language=en}}</ref>

* The Humboldt-Meitner Award in Atomic and Molecular Physics (The Humboldt Foundation, Germany) (2009)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nonlinear Filtering of Quantum Noise for Sensing and Work – TAMU Physics & Astronomy |url=https://physics.tamu.edu/events/nonlinear-filtering-of-quantum-noise-for-sensing-and-work/ |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=physics.tamu.edu}}</ref>

* Member, [[Academia Europaea]] (2023)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Kurizki Gershon |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kurizki_Gershon |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

==Books==
His book The Quantum Matrix (Oxford University Press, 2020), co-authored with Goren Gordon, pairs a graphic-novel narrative built around a quantum superhero named Henry Bar with underlying physics explanations.<ref>{{cite web |last=Arcon |first=Danielle |date=2020-12-30 |title=The Quantum Matrix: Henry Bar's Perilous Struggle for Quantum Coherence |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/culture/the-quantum-matrix-henry-bars-perilous-struggle-for-quantum-coherence/4012682.article |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=Chemistry World }}</ref> It renders scientific, philosophical and poetic descriptions of the world. A second book, ''Thermodynamics and Control of Open Quantum Systems'' (Cambridge University Press, 2022), co-authored with Abraham G. Kofman, is a 450-page treatment of open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics, covering dynamical control, quantum measurements, decoherence, quantum heat engines, and quantum refrigerators, of particular interest to researchers working in the field.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kurizki |first1=Gershon |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/thermodynamics-and-control-of-open-quantum-systems/413DEC3CB5CCC4665EEE86777EC19CD5 |title=Thermodynamics and Control of Open Quantum Systems |last2=Kofman |first2=Abraham G. |date=2022 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-17541-9 |location=Cambridge}}</ref>

== Poetry and philosophical writing ==
Alongside his scientific career, Gershon Kurizki has published philosophical essays combined with poetry in literary and philosophical magazines and books:

In the literary-philosophical magazine The New Rainbow (Keshet hahadasha):

* "On the reality of time" 11 (2005)
* "Rapture at the sight of an atom" 14 (2005)
* "On infinity and eternity - when will Achilles overtake the turtle?" 16 (2006)
* "Redemption through wisdom - Spinoza's gospel and science" 19 (2007)
* "The observer and the world" 21 (2007)

His book The Quantum Matrix similarly combines scientific ideas with narrative and philosophical elements.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kurizki |first1=Gershon |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/thermodynamics-and-control-of-open-quantum-systems/413DEC3CB5CCC4665EEE86777EC19CD5 |title=Thermodynamics and Control of Open Quantum Systems |last2=Kofman |first2=Abraham G. |date=2022 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-17541-9 |location=Cambridge}}</ref>
